newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs approve common positions on inland waterways.
newsitem.headline: MEPs approve common positions on inland waterways.

text.p: The Transport Council's common positions on restructuring, liberalising and promoting inland waterway transport won approval from MEPs on Tuesday -- albeit with two amendments.

When EU transport ministers approved proposal COM(95)199 covering these three aspects of the European Union's inland waterways earlier this year, they disregarded most of the amendments which the European Parliament had requested at first reading (cooperation procedure).

At second reading, Dutch Europe of Nations MEP Leen van der Waal criticised Council's decision not to finance beyond the end of 1996 a programme designed to restructure the sector by reducing overcapacity.
Adopting his report on the proposals, MEPs reinstated their earlier demand for an extra scrapping scheme for the tanker sector, where overcapacity is estimated at 20 percent.
Ministers had accepted approved the Commission's proposal for liberalising the inland waterways sector by 2000 by gradually abolishing the system of chartering by rotation.
While this pleased MEPs, they insisted the member states should introduce accompanying social measures for carriers which close down their business.
Commissioner Hans van den Broek told MEPs on Monday night that the Commission could not go along with either amendment.
